methodological_rigor.justification: Solid, well-controlled methodology. Integrates multi-omic profiling (RNA-seq, DNA methylation EPIC arrays, ATAC-seq, proteomics) with appropriate bioinformatics (DESeq2, limma, DiffBind with FDR correction). Patient cohort validation (BeatAML, TCGA, BLUEPRINT). Functional assays include cell viability, qPCR, flow cytometry. Multiple replicates (n=3 biological). Limitations acknowledged: Nanaomycin A selectivity is imperfect (quinone scaffold off-target effects); accessibility changes correlative, not definitively causal.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: LoE 2b: cell line mechanistic study with patient cohort validation. Clinical relevance plausible. DNMT3B overexpression associated with poor prognosis in defined AML subtypes (CEBPA-, NPM1-mutant). Proposed DNMT3B + venetoclax combination is rational but not yet clinically tested. Translational path described but requires in vivo validation.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods comprehensive and reproducible with detailed bioinformatic parameter sets (DESeq2 v1.40.2, DiffBind v3.8.0). Experimental design clear. Supplementary tables (S1-S11) referenced. Adherence to ARRIVE/REMARK standards strong but data availability statement absent from main text.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel mechanistic integration of DNMT3B's role in AML-specific epigenetic regulation. Focus on DNMT3B (vs DNMT3A) overexpression and enhancer-driven activation is new. Link to apoptotic rewiring and venetoclax sensitization represents meaningful mechanistic advance.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured, clearly written. Methods detailed and reproducible. Complex multi-omic data effectively communicated through figures. Some sections dense but logical organization maintained throughout.

key_strengths: Comprehensive multi-omic integration (RNA-seq, DNA methylation, ATAC-seq, proteomics) with appropriate statistical correction.
Patient cohort validation showing clinical relevance of DNMT3B expression across AML subtypes.
Clear mechanistic pathway: enhancer-driven overexpression→epigenetic remodeling→apoptotic priming→venetoclax sensitization.
Explicit acknowledgment of Nanaomycin A limitations and conservative interpretation of causality.
key_concerns: Nanaomycin A not fully selective; quinone scaffold induces off-target oxidative stress independent of DNMT3B.
ATAC-seq and methylation changes correlative; direct occupancy studies (ChIP-seq, CUT&RUN) not performed.
Apoptotic priming inferred from transcriptional readouts; functional mitochondrial priming assays (BH3 profiling) not included.
Venetoclax sensitization demonstrated only in cell lines; in vivo and primary AML validation needed.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Rigorous multi-omic mechanistic study with patient validation. LoE 2b. Solid methodology with acknowledged limitations. Ready for publication with minor data availability clarification.
